# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands have found: a display I can't read, a light whose state I don't reach, one plate engraved with a single symbol (which I *can* feel — the mark is real under my fingers), and three wires at positions 1–3 whose colours tell me nothing. My only possible action is `cut` at position 1, 2 or 3, so whatever the manual says must ultimately resolve to "cut wire N".

Tracing the channels: Mute holds the manual but cannot speak — Mute reaches Deaf only by gesture. Deaf sees the bomb (colours, the display, the printed plate) and can speak, which reaches me. So the manual's knowledge reaches me only as Mute → gesture → Deaf → speech → me. I should start both ends of that chain now: give Mute my tactile description of the engraving so they can look it up, and signal Deaf to speak what they see once they have the manual's questions.

To Mute I'll describe the engraved mark as my fingers find it, list everything I can and cannot feel, and ask them to route the manual's rules through Deaf. To Deaf I'll send a simple attention-and-request gesture — no shared code exists yet, so I just need Deaf to know I'm here and asking, since Deaf's spoken reply at the end of this round is the first thing I'll ever receive.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I can touch the bomb, nothing else. Under my fingers: a display I cannot read, a light whose state I cannot feel, one plate engraved with a single symbol, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3 - they give me no colour or texture difference, only count and position. The engraved symbol feels like a tight cluster of five or six small round dots bunched together in the middle, like a bunch of grapes or a paw print - all circles, no straight lines, about thumbnail-sized. Please look that up in the manual. The only action I have is cutting wire 1, 2 or 3, so whatever the manual says must end as cut wire N. You cannot speak, so please gesture the manual's rules and questions to Deaf, and Deaf can speak them to me - that is the only path the manual has to my hands.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫴", "👉"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. I see the bomb: display reads 0, light is off, plate is engraved with a question mark, and there are three wires. Feel for them: wire 1 is the one nearest the display, then wire 2, then wire 3; nearest is red, middle blue, last green, though you cannot see colour. Protocol: Mute has the manual but cannot speak, and you two have no channel between you. So speak your findings aloud, Mute hears them, Mute gestures them to me, and I relay instructions to you by speech. I cannot hear you, so gesture me anything meant for me alone: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Feel the bomb now and confirm the display, light, plate and three wires, and describe by voice anything you feel that I might not see: buttons, batteries, markings. Do not cut anything until an instruction from me.

What I learned: Deaf sees the bomb and has named my engraving — the dot-cluster under my fingers is a question mark — plus display reads 0, light is off, and the wires run red/blue/green at positions 1/2/3, wire 1 nearest the display. Deaf also fixed a yes/no code for me: thumbs up/down, since my voice can never reach Deaf's ears. Deaf ordered no cutting until an instruction arrives — correct, I have zero basis to choose a wire yet.

Checking my own hands once more: my board shows only display, light, plate, three wires. No buttons, no batteries, nothing else under my fingers — and the display's reading and the light's state are simply not tactile, so I can confirm the plate and wires but not those two.

Topology check: Mute (manual) cannot speak; Deaf cannot hear. So the manual reaches me only as Mute → gesture → Deaf → speech → me, and my touch facts reach Deaf only the same way — my voice can only ever land on Mute. My named gesture lands on Deaf this very round (Deaf acts after me), so the 👍 confirmation arrives in time; my speech to Mute cannot land until Mute's next turn (Mute already went this round), so the full inventory and lookup request ride together for round 3. I cut nothing.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. News from Deaf, relayed to me by speech since you could not hear it: the symbol engraved on the plate is a question mark, the display reads 0, the light is off, and the wires are red at position 1 (nearest the display), blue at 2, green at 3. My full touch inventory, final: one plate with a single engraved symbol, three wires in a row at positions 1, 2, 3 with wire 1 nearest the display, and a display and a light whose states I cannot feel at all. Nothing else is under my fingers - no buttons, no batteries, no other markings or parts. Deaf has ordered me not to cut until Deaf instructs. Please search the manual for the rule matching this configuration: display 0, light off, question-mark plate, wires red/blue/green at 1/2/3 nearest-display-first. Gesture whatever the manual concludes to Deaf, and ask Deaf to speak me the instruction as cut wire N. Also please relay to Deaf by gesture: Blind confirms by touch the plate and the three wires; Blind cannot feel the display or light states; Blind feels no other components.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. Decoded instruction from Mute, via gesture: cut wire 3. Anchor it by touch: the bomb has a display, then a plate, then a row of exactly three wires. Wire 1 is nearest the display, wire 3 is the farthest from the display, the last one in the row. Do this now: first feel and confirm you find the display, the engraved plate, and exactly three wires in a row. If all of that matches, cut wire 3, the one farthest from the display. If anything does not match — a missing part, a fourth wire, a button I did not report — do not cut. Instead gesture me thumbs down and speak aloud what you feel so Mute can hear it. After you cut, speak aloud everything that changes: any number on the display, whether a light comes on, any sound, so Mute hears it and can instruct us further.

Verification against Deaf's checklist, part by part under my fingers: the display is there, the engraved plate is there with its single symbol, and there are exactly three wires in a row — no fourth wire, no button, no unreported part. The light sits between display and plate, but Deaf reported the light from the start, so it is not a surprise component. The order also anchors correctly: display at one end, plate next to the wires, wires last — so wire 3, farthest from the display, is the last one in the row under my hand. Every condition Deaf set for cutting is met, and the instruction chain Mute → gesture → Deaf → speech is the only path the manual's rule could have travelled to me; I have no independent way to check it, and no better information. I cut wire 3 now.

Deaf cannot hear my report, so the thumbs-up carries "matched, proceeding" on the agreed code — it lands on Deaf this same round since Deaf speaks after me. Mute already went this round, so my spoken report arrives next round: I'll tell Mute the verification passed and the cut is made, and next turn, once the board shows me what changed, I'll report every change for the manual-checking to continue.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Deaf's relayed instruction received: cut wire 3. I verified every anchor by touch first - display present, plate present with its single engraved symbol, exactly three wires in a row, wire 3 farthest from the display, no extra parts - and everything matched Deaf's description, so I have cut wire 3. Next round I will report every change my hands can find and whatever Deaf speaks me about the display and light, so you can check the manual for the next step. Please standby with the manual and relay anything Deaf gestures you to me if I need correcting.")
```
